headline: Approved Yellen Pines housing tax increment deal as amended, $1,400,000 bonds for 103 Maine Avenue, and data center moratorium extension; Project HOPE failed.
summary: Yellen Pines, a housing tax increment financing deal, was approved as amended by a 5-3 vote. Up to $1,400,000 in bonds for land at 103 Maine Avenue was approved, and a moratorium on data centers was extended. A motion to pass the $300,000 Project HOPE resolve failed, and $7,000 in opioid settlement funds was approved for The Together Place.
decisions: Elected Councilor Carson as chair pro tem.
Approved minutes of the September 14, 2026 regular meeting and three Business and Economic Development Committee meetings.
Approved a municipal quitclaim deed for real estate at 37 Nelson Street.
Directed the City Manager to take possession of 290 Pearl Street.
Approved renaming Lilac Avenue to Virginia Lane.
Approved renaming Pleasant View Street to Pleasant View Avenue.
Approved renewal of the agreement with Lyft Inc. d/b/a LYFT for service at Bangor International Airport.
Approved renewal of the agreement with Raiser, LLC, d/b/a UBER, for service at Bangor International Airport.
Motion to postpone the $300,000 Project HOPE resolve to October 5, 2026 failed, 3-5.
Motion to pass the Project HOPE resolve was recorded as failed, although the minutes show an 8-0 vote.
Passed the moratorium extension ordinance on data centers, 8-0.
Accepted and appropriated an airport improvement grant for rehabilitation of Taxiway A and Taxiway M at Bangor International Airport.
Approved $7,000 from opioid settlement funds for The Together Place, 6-1.
Approved amending Council Resolve 26-195, the total school budget for the Bangor School Department.
Approved up to $1,400,000 in bonds and a tax levy for 103 Maine Avenue; minutes record a 7-1 vote with inconsistent roll call lists.
Found that Councilor Beck had a conflict of interest on the Evenrood's permit.
Approved special amusement permit for Evenrood's, 25 Broad Street.
Approved appointing nominees to various boards, commissions and committees.
Approved amending the Yellen Pines item by substitution.
Motion to postpone the Yellen Pines item to the October 5, 2026 Council Workshop failed, 4-4.
Motion to postpone the Yellen Pines item indefinitely failed, 3-5.
Approved the Yellen Pines application, development program, and credit enhancement agreement as amended, 5-3.
Approved a resolution recognizing the cooperative partnership between the City of Bangor and the Penobscot Job Corps Center.

Two of you requested the Environmental Review Record for this project last week. The City

September 28, 2026
To: Members of the Bangor City Council
From: Jacqueline Smallwood, Bangor resident
RE: Yellen Pines— Request to Postpone Tonight' s Vote
I am asking you to postponetonight' s vote until three specific, documentedproblems are resolved. This letter
lays out those problems in more detail than I have time for at the podium, with copies of the underlying
documents attachedso you havethem in handtonight, not just my summary of them.
ONE— THE FEDERAL ENVIRONMENTAL NOTICE HAS THE WRONG ADDRESS
The City' s own Combined Notice of Finding of No Significant Impact and Notice of Intent to Request
Release of Funds, last updated September 1, 2026, certifies environmental clearance for" a 30- unit supportive
housing facility for chronically homeless individuals at 55 Cleveland St." That is not this project. Every TIF
order, the Credit EnhancementAgreement, andthe City' s own Affordable Housing TIF application submitted
to MaineHousing all identify the site as 205 Corporate Drive. A copy of the notice is attached.If the certified
environmental clearance is for a different address, then no valid clearance currently exists for the project you
are being asked to approve tonight.
TWO— THIS PROJECT DOES NOT HAVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW IT IS REQUIRED
TO HAVE, AND WHAT EXISTS HAS A POTENTIAL ENGINEERING PROBLEM
At leasttwo councilors requesteda copy of the Environmental Review Record( NEPA Study) last week
beforetonight'smeetinganddidnotreceiveit. Under24CFRPart58,theCityisthe"responsibleentity"
HUD has delegated this review to— the City decides its own environmental classification, conductsthe
review, and simply certifies the result to HUD. HUD doesnot independently re-verify the substanceof that
certification. In practice, that meansthe only real check on whether the City got this right is the public and
this Council asking to seethe work. The Council was denied accessto a document HUD' s own rules require
the City to make public.
To be clear, I am not an engineer in any form, however an independentengineering review of the project's
own stormwater plans has identified a specific, checkableproblem with that work. The plans call for capping
the existing 18-inch storm drain that currently carries part of this site'srunoff under Maine Avenue, and
routing all of that flow— plus the site' s own increased runoff from new pavement and roofing— through the
remaining 30- inch pipe at Analysis Point 1. Using the developer' s own engineer' s flow data( Sevee& Mahar
Engineers, cited to page409 of the June 16Planning Board minutes), the 25-year storm flow through that
single pipe increases from 25. 12 cfs before development to 31. 51 cfs after— roughly a 25 percent increase.
Neither the sealedplans nor the topographic survey provide a downstream invert elevation for that pipe—
only the upstream elevation is documented. Without it, nobody can calculate the pipe's actual slope, and
without the slope, nobody can confirm it can carry the increasedflow without backing up. Using Manning' s
Equation with a standardfriction factor for corrugated plastic pipe( Chow, 1959),the pipe would needa
minimum slope of 1.29 percent to carry the 10-year storm and 2.01 percent to carry the 25-year storm—
meaningthedownstreamendneedsto sit ator below 153.15feetand152.60feetrespectively.Nobodyhas
shown that it does.If it doesnot, water backs up, and becausethis drains toward Maine Avenue, that is a
road-floodingrisk. This gapwasmissedby boththeapplicant'sown sealingengineerandtheCity'sownplan
reviewer. A copy of the independentengineering letter is attached.
I havequestionsasto how,this projectwasclassifiedunderPart58.Newconstructionof a 30-unit building
on a single site does not fit any of the Categorical Exclusion Categories listed at 24 CFR 58. 35( a)— that
provisioncoversrehabilitationofexistingbuildings,acquisitionof existingstructures,or newconstruction
capped at four units per site. This project is none of those. Separately, 58. 35( c) requires full environmental
2. Produce the Environmental Review Record that at least two Council members have already requested;

and when Map/Lot R25-001-A was created,that 205 Corporate Drive is actually fully covered by a
federal release— not simply that a releaseexists somewherein the samegeneral area; supportedby
licensed professionals.
4. Require the developer to produce the missing downstream pipe elevation and slope calculation, verified
independently by City engineering staff, before this agreementis finalized; and
5. Explain, on the record, why the City' s own Planning Board packet for this project contains a deedthat has
never been documentedascovering this parcel, and produce the subdivision paperwork connecting it to
Map/Lot R25-001-A if one exists.
If theseitems cannot be resolved satisfactorily, I intend to pursue this directly with HUD, including through
the formal objection processunder 24 CFR 58.76 and, if warranted, a referral to HUD' s Office of Inspector
General. The HUD objection window is limited and runs 15 days from your Sept. 16 submission. I am
preparedto file within that window if there is no immediate responseback.
Thank you for your time and attention to this.

BACKGROUND
Two City Councilors requested this Environmental Assessment/ Environmental Review Record last week.
The City delivered it today at 2: 30 PM, for a 5: 15 PM meeting— roughly three hours to review a 58- page
federal compliance document before a vote on a 30-year agreement. The document was preparedand certified
by Robyn Stanicki, who is listed asboth the RE Preparer and the Certifying Officer for this review—
meaning the sameindividual who conductedthe review also certified that it was done correctly, with no
independentcheck built into the City' s own process.
KEY FINDINGS
1. The document' s own" Project Location" field lists the wrong address. Page2 states" Project Location:
55 Cleveland Street, Bangor, ME 04401." This is not limited to the public notice previously identified—
it is the formal location field in the underlying federal environmental review record itself.
2. The document contradicts itself internally. Despite the Project Location field above, the substantive
analysis throughout the same document repeatedly identifies the site as 205 Corporate Drive: the
Conformance with Plans" fmding( page 10), the" Summary of Findings and Conclusions"( page 16), the
Historic Preservation Area of Potential Effect( page 47), and the filename of the Phase I Environmental
Site Assessment itself(" Phase 1 ESA- Corporate Drive Bangor ME"). The substantive technical work
appears to have been conducted for the correct site; the formal location field— the onethat generatedthe
public notice— was not corrected to match.
3. A new, unexplained acquisition date. Page3 statesthe site" was acquired by the City from the U.S.
government in 1964." This date matchesnone of the four deedsidentified in this project's chain of title
1968, 1969, 1996, or 2002), and is not reconciled anywhere in the document.
4. The document never addresses the FAA/ aviation land- restriction question. The" Additional Location
Information" section( page 2) describes the site' s history in detail— a pump station, Air Force base
operations, military housing, barracks buildings, hangars— and states plainly that" recognized
environmental conditions( RECs) associated with the historical use of the site were identified." Despite
this, the document never once addresseswhether the site remains subject to FAA use restrictions or grant
assuranceobligations tied to that samehistory. The reviewer clearly knew enough about the
military/ aviation history to write about it at length, but never connectedit to the federal land-use question.
5. Total project cost does not match other City- published figures. This document lists" Estimated Total
Project Cost: $ 12, 122, 745. 00"— different from the$ 11, 185, 881 figure in the FONSI/ Release of Funds
notice and the approximately$ 11.2 million figure reported by the Bangor Daily News.
6. Disclosed soil contamination, mitigated but real. A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment and follow-
up soil testing identified PFOS, arsenic, and chromium at levels exceeding residential screening
guidelines( though below construction-worker action levels). The document attributes the arsenicto
natural background conditions and proposesmitigation through soil removal and clean fill, to be self-
documented by Bangor Housing and monitored by the City reviewing that same documentation.
7. Tribal historic preservation consultation shows no response, not agreement. The Mi' kmaq Nation,
Passamaquoddy,and PenobscotNation are eachmarked" ResponsePeriod Elapsed" under Section 106
consultation. Under the regulation, non-responseafter the required period may be treated asno objection
but this is not the same as affirmative concurrence.

RE: Bangor Housing Development Corporation- Yellen Pines
A consulting engineer has raised a technical objection to the engineering plans submitted
by Bangor Housing Development Corporation for the Yellen Pines project located at 205
Corporate Drive, Bangor, Maine, 04401. This is in reference to the seated plans prepared by
Sevee& Mahar Engineers( SME), Dated May 28th, 2026. It is the opinion of the Engineer that
these plans and associatedstormwater report do not adequatelyanalyzeor address
adverse impacts to adjacent properties or downstream structures as a result of this
project.
The project narrative indicates that the 18- inch Corrugated Metal Pipe ( CMP) storm drain
